status: PLAN ONLY. No video has been recorded. Durations are intended, not measured against a take. Every beat is an action that exists in the repository today and was performed in a desktop browser against a local server. No beat shows a Fire TV device or the Fire TV emulator, because no APK has been built.
title: Mercury: Fire TV Incident Commander
note: words_count and words_per_minute are computed from narration_text by the generator. They describe the script, not a recording.

beats.narration_text: An incident starts. Somebody asks what broke, and the first answer everyone reaches for is: what did we just deploy. Half the time that is the wrong question, and reverting on it costs an hour.
beats.visual_action: Cold open on the loaded cockpit at 1920x1080 in a desktop browser. No click yet.

beats.narration_text: Mercury answers before anyone clicks, and its most common answer is a refusal. Against eleven hundred and sixty labelled incidents it sees a real anomaly and names nobody eighty one percent of the time. That is the product: do not revert anything, this is not a deploy.
beats.visual_action: Reload the page. The hero renders the correlator's verdict and the anomaly factor as the large figure. Do not click anything yet.

beats.narration_text: Here is the refusal that matters. Six changes landed in the hour before this spike started. Nothing in a metric series says which of them did it, so Mercury names none of them and the rollback stays disabled.
beats.visual_action: Press release-train. The hero reads Do not revert on this, names the number of changes in the window, and both rollback buttons stay disabled with their reason lines visible.

beats.narration_text: It names a change only when exactly one landed in the window. And when it does, it prints its own odds: against that same corpus the commit it names is the one that caused the reading fifty two percent of the time, over one hundred and thirteen namings. The screen says so beside the name.
beats.visual_action: Press checkout-api. The hero names the commit, quotes its message, and the line under it reads the measured precision and the number of namings it was measured over.

beats.narration_text: Both halves of that answer say where they came from, next to the number rather than under the fold. The metric series is generated locally and the badge in the card reads OFFLINE FIXTURE. The commits are real, read from the checkout.
beats.visual_action: Hold on the two source badges inside the hero card beside the anomaly factor, OFFLINE FIXTURE against metric series and LIVE against commit history. Do not scroll.

beats.narration_text: The remote moves in space, not down a list. Focus jumps to the nearest control in the direction pressed, disabled controls are skipped rather than focused, and Back returns to the wall before it would ever close the application.
beats.visual_action: Press Right, Right, Down, Right, Left, then Enter on the Delivery velocity tile and Escape. The Focused label and the BACK legend change with each press.

beats.narration_text: One screen, two kinds of truth. The velocity panel is serving a recording because no GitHub token is set, and says so. The spend panel, on a machine with credentials, is a live Cost Explorer read, and says that too.
beats.visual_action: Load DORA velocity, then scan AWS spend. Compare the OFFLINE FIXTURE badge against the LIVE aws-cost-explorer badge. Do not read live spend figures aloud.

beats.narration_text: The only irreversible control on the screen refuses in plain words when the governance secret is missing. It does not fail silently and it does not pretend.
beats.visual_action: Go back to checkout-api. With the Secret field empty, press Stage governed rollback. The incident panel shows the refusal text.

beats.narration_text: With the secret, staging mints a single-use token bound to a hash of exactly this rollback. Change the target afterwards and the token stops applying.
beats.visual_action: Type the secret, stage again. Show PENDING_CONFIRMATION, the payload hash, the lease countdown as the hero figure, and Confirm becoming enabled.

beats.narration_text: Governance passes, and the product says out loud what it did not do. No deployment pipeline was contacted. Press it again and the server refuses by name: the token was valid once.
beats.visual_action: Press Confirm rollback and read the EXECUTED output verbatim, including the sentence stating no pipeline was contacted. Press it a second time and show the 409 NOT_PENDING denial.

beats.narration_text: What is not built: no APK exists, the Kotlin has never been compiled, and nothing has run on Fire TV hardware. The refusals, the correlation and the governance were driven live here. The device was not.
beats.visual_action: Cut to docs/FIRE_TV_BUILD.md open on the recorded build failure.
